# Preface {.unnumbered}

This report documents the applications shipped with OpenPFC 0.2: what each one
solves, how it is discretised, how it is verified, and — where it has been
measured — how it scales.

Every chapter follows the same shape. The governing equations come first, in
the form a physicist would write them. The discrete formulation follows: for
the spectral applications that means the reciprocal-space symbol, and for the
finite-difference applications the stencil and update rule. Each chapter then
states what is actually verified in the test suite, so a claim in this report
can be traced to an assertion in the repository.

The report is written in Quarto. It has no compute engine: the scalability
figures are committed SVGs regenerated by `figures/make_figures.py` from the
CSV files under `data/`, which are themselves transcribed from
[`docs/hpc/lumi_gpu_scaling.md`](../hpc/lumi_gpu_scaling.md).

```bash
quarto render docs/report          # HTML
quarto render docs/report --to pdf # PDF
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Status

This is a first draft. The mathematics and verification sections are complete
for every shipped application. The scalability chapter covers the three models
that have been measured on LUMI-G; the remaining applications are marked as
unmeasured rather than estimated.
:::
